description: PART C - make the navigation feel like a professional mobile trading app (CoinDCX-style bottom tab bar) instead of the top hamburger, and add a Help section that lets a user email info@ARVcoin.com. USER REQUEST (steering): on mobile all the main destinations should sit in a fixed bottom bar (Home/Overview, Market/Trade, History, Wallet, Portfolio, etc.) tappable to navigate directly; the current three-line hamburger looks unprofessional. Also add a Help/support section reachable to email info@ARVcoin.com for problems. Nav is generated in js/ui.js mountNav(); styled in css/core.css. This is additive UI - it does not touch money or price logic. Independent of FEAT-002/003 but shares js/ui.js, so land after them to avoid churn.
steps: In js/ui.js mountNav(): keep the existing top nav for desktop, but ADD a fixed bottom tab bar for mobile (CoinDCX-style). Build it from the same NAV array (or a curated subset of primary destinations: Overview/Home index.html, Trade trade.html, Wallet dashboard.html, Portfolio portfolio.html, History transactions.html) plus respect the auth flag (auth-only tabs shown only when user is signed in; for signed-out users show Home/Trade/Sign in). Each tab: an icon (inline SVG or an existing icon/emoji-free glyph consistent with the design) + a short label, with the current page marked .on (reuse the currentPage() helper). Render into a new container e.g. <nav class='tabbar' data-tabbar> ... </nav> appended to the nav host or body.

Make the bottom tab bar mobile-only via CSS: visible (display:flex, fixed bottom, full width, safe-area inset padding) under the existing mobile breakpoint (the codebase uses ~760px in ui.js mountHero small check and likely in core.css); hidden on desktop. On mobile, hide/allow the old hamburger nav-toggle so the primary navigation is the bottom bar (keep the top brand + nav ticker + account/sign-out reachable; the hamburger can be removed on mobile or repurposed for the secondary items like Deposit/Withdraw/Refer/Profile/Help that don't fit in the bottom bar). Ensure page content has bottom padding so the fixed bar never overlaps the footer/last elements on mobile.

Add matching CSS to css/core.css: a .tabbar block styled in the silver-on-black design (dark background, subtle top border, muted icons, active tab highlighted like the existing .on state), tab items evenly spaced, touch-friendly hit targets (>=44px), and a body/main padding-bottom on mobile so nothing is hidden behind the bar. Reuse existing colour variables/classes where present. Do NOT break the desktop top nav.

Add a Help/support entry point: (a) add a 'Help' link/tab (in the bottom bar overflow/secondary menu and/or the footer) that goes to a support affordance, and (b) provide a way to email info@ARVcoin.com - simplest robust approach with no backend change: a mailto:info@ARVcoin.com link (e.g. 'Contact support' button) with a sensible default subject like 'ARV Coin support request'. Place a clear Help/Support section: add it to mountFooter() in js/ui.js (a new 'Help' column or a 'Contact support' line with the mailto), AND surface a Help item in the mobile secondary menu. Keep the email address exactly info@ARVcoin.com.

Verify the nav still mounts for both signed-in and signed-out users (mountNav takes user | null). Ensure no auth-only destination is exposed to signed-out users in the bottom bar. Keep the existing sign-out button behaviour working.
Run env -u NODE_OPTIONS node --check on js/ui.js and any other changed js file. Since this is pure DOM-string generation + CSS, confirm parse-clean and reason about the markup by reading it.
acceptance_criteria: On mobile widths a fixed bottom tab bar (CoinDCX-style) provides direct navigation to the primary destinations (Overview, Trade, Wallet, Portfolio, History), with the current page highlighted; auth-only tabs only appear when signed in.
The bottom bar is hidden on desktop (the existing top nav remains the desktop navigation); page content is padded so the fixed bar does not overlap content on mobile.
A Help/Support affordance exists (footer section and/or mobile secondary menu) with a working mailto to info@ARVcoin.com.
Signed-out users are never shown auth-only destinations; sign-out still works.
env -u NODE_OPTIONS node --check passes on js/ui.js and other changed js files; silver-on-black design preserved, no money/price logic touched.
verification: Read mountNav()/mountFooter() output markup and the .tabbar CSS to confirm mobile-only display, auth gating, and the mailto target.
findings: Implemented purely additive UI in js/ui.js + css/core.css; no money/PHP touched. (1) mountNav() now appends a fixed bottom tab bar via tabbarMarkup(user, here): a new TABS subset (Overview/Trade/Wallet/Portfolio/History) with inline monochrome SVG icons (TAB_ICONS, currentColor). Auth-only tabs (Wallet/Portfolio/History) gated on `user`; signed-out users get Overview+Trade + a Sign in tab, signed-in users get an Account tab appended (dedup so bar stays 5 even targets). Current page marked .on reusing currentPage(). Rendered as <nav class='tabbar' data-tabbar aria-label='Primary'>. (2) CSS: .tabbar hidden by default (desktop keeps top .nav); shown flex/fixed-bottom only at max-width:760px with env(safe-area-inset-bottom) padding, >=52px touch targets, active .on lit like nav's .on (var(--s-0) + drop-shadow). body gets padding-bottom on mobile so the bar never overlaps footer/content. Added .tabbar to the print display:none rule. (3) Help/support: SUPPORT_EMAIL='info@ARVcoin.com' (exact) + SUPPORT_MAILTO with subject 'ARV Coin support request'. New 'Help & support' footer column (Contact support + the raw email + How the price works); foot-grid bumped from 1.6fr repeat(3,1fr) to repeat(4,1fr) (degrades to 1fr/2col at existing 1080/660 breakpoints). Also a .nav-help link inside .nav-links, display:none on desktop, display:block at <=760px so it surfaces in the mobile hamburger 'More' overflow. Old hamburger relabelled aria-label='More' (kept for secondary items). VERIFY: env -u NODE_OPTIONS node --check js/ui.js -> parse OK. All em dashes present are pre-existing in surrounding copy; my new comment uses a hyphen. NOTE: responsive/visual behaviour reasoned from markup+CSS only (no browser in sandbox); 760px tabbar breakpoint vs the existing 880px hamburger breakpoint means between 761-880px the top hamburger is the nav (unchanged legacy behaviour) and the tabbar is mobile (<=760px) as instructed.
